skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: At T2, before any question, the lawyer said the firm represents the Committee and the company, not the witness, and cannot give legal advice.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: T2 says the privilege belongs to the company, which may decide to share what is said, including with the government.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: No ground rules on speculation, clarification or recollection versus uncertainty; the interview moved straight into questions at T4.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: T2 ends with 'Any questions?' and the witness confirms at T3 that he understands he is not the interviewer's client.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: T150 asked whether anything was missed and T158 gave confidentiality and document-retention instructions, but no next steps were stated.

moments.text: We represent the Committee and the company, not you personally. We're not your attorney and can't give you legal advice.
the privilege belongs to the company, and the company may decide to share what you tell us with others, including the government.
I understand you're not my lawyer.
First substantive question came with no explanation of how the interview would proceed or how to handle speculation.
Asked whether there is anything the Committee should know that was not asked.
Please keep any documents related to this, and don't discuss this interview with anyone.

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: Open invitations at T12, T24, T32 and T46 let the witness walk through events before narrowing.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: Moves from general to specific, for example T46 to T48 to T50 on Raptor I, though chronology jumps between 1997, 1999, 2000 and 2001.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Most questions are single and clear, such as T122; a few, like T30, are broader than needed.

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: Stays polite and in control through challenges such as T82 and T136, though T82 is pointed.

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: Departs from the outline to pursue the foundation at T69 to T75, the Southampton terms at T89, and the Chewco note at T132.

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.
skills.reason: Challenged the Chewco and Andy contradictions well at T121 to T137, but left evasive key answers at T45, T93, T97, T149 and T157 unchallenged.

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.
skills.reason: Pins down who negotiated, amounts and dates, such as Causey's group at T27, Glisan at T55 and the $4.5 million on May 1 at T80.

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.
skills.reason: Used documents to refresh memory at T72, T98 and T132, and asked for figures again at T76 to T80.

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.
skills.reason: Asked who decided at T86 and T104, but did not test how the witness knew of Skilling's approval at T41 or the payment decision at T139.

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.
skills.reason: T152 asked who else to speak with, and the witness named Causey, Buy, Glisan, Kopper and the firms, but none was pursued further.

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.description: Identifies other documents such as communications, reports, notes, or other relevant records.
skills.reason: T154 and T156 asked for documents and personal notes or emails, though the follow-up on the personal files was thin.

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.description: Examines how certain the witness is about their memory or a fact.
skills.reason: Rarely asked how sure the witness was; accepted I don't recall at T45 and I may have at T97 without testing them.

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.description: Recognizes material responses and follows up on them.
skills.reason: Nine key leads were never followed up, including T53, T57, T149 and T157, which caps the score at 2.

skills.reason: The interview established who, when and how for the Southampton investment (T72 to T96), the Chewco buyout price (T126 to T130) and the LJM2 returns.

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.reason: When the witness could not recall, documents were used: the agreement at T74, the investor report at T100 and the Kopper note at T132.

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.reason: The interviewer asked who set the Southampton terms (T88), but did not probe how the witness knew Skilling told the Board (T41) or what he personally saw.

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.reason: T152 asked who else to speak with, and the witness named Causey, Buy, Glisan, Kopper, Andersen and Vinson and Elkins.

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.reason: T154 and T156 asked about documents and personal notes or emails, though the interviewer did not press further on the personal records.

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.reason: T62 asked for an approximation and T64 pressed for a number; T79 and T80 tested a few million against a specific figure. The I don't recall answers at T45 and T53 were not tested.

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.reason: Many material answers were followed up, but key leads at T53 and T157 were never pursued, which caps this skill at 2.

skills.name: Effective Selection
skills.reason: The Southampton agreement (T72), LJM2 investor report (T98) and Kopper note (T132) were shown with context, and the witness was asked to confirm each (T73, T99).

skills.name: Narrative
skills.reason: The witness gave his account first (T69 to T71 and T97) before the documents were shown at T72 and T98.

skills.name: Accuracy
skills.reason: Descriptions at T74 (the 25,000 contribution), T80 (May 1 and 4.5 million), T100 (193, 278 and 2,500 percent) and T132 ($10.5 million) match the document contents.

skills.name: Avoid Initial Conclusion
skills.reason: Documents were presented neutrally, asking Is that accurate? at T80 and Are those the figures? at T100, though T82 set the return against the earlier Board statement.

skills.name: Fairness
skills.reason: The witness was given room to explain at T83, T101, T117 and T137, and T116 and T136 invited him to reconcile the figures.

tips: When a witness says something may have happened, ask: What exactly did you say or do, to whom, and when, before moving on?
When a witness admits a control failure, ask: Which approvals were signed after closing, which deals were they, and who knew the deal had already closed?
